L263: # DeepSeek Harness
L264: 
L265: English | cite117†中文 L266: 
L267: DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) is an open-source agent harness developed by cite143†DeepSeek AI†deepseek.com .
L268: 
L269: It is built on an everything-is-a-plugin architecture and powered by cite144†Cordis , whose design is described in cite145†A Programming Paradigm for Spatiotemporal Composability†arxiv.org .
L270: 
L271: Documentation: cite146†https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/†deepseek-harness.github.io L272: ## Developer preview
L273: 
L274: DeepSeek Harness is in developer preview and iterating rapidly. THERE WILL BE COMPATIBILITY-BREAKING CHANGES.
L275: 
L276: Review the cite119†safety notice before running the project.
L277: 
L278: ## Run
L279: ### Run from `npm`
L280: 
L281: Install `Node.js`, then run:
L282: 
L283:     npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web
L284: 
L285: The command starts the Web UI at `http://127.0.0.1:3080` by default and opens it in the default browser for a local launch. An SSH launch only prints the host URL because the SSH client or editor owns the local forwarded address. Pass `--no-open` to run the server without opening a browser. See cite147†Web UI guide .
L286: ### Run from source
L287: 
L288: To run from a repository checkout:
L289: 
L290:     git clone https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness.git
L291:     cd deepseek-harness
L292:     pnpm install
L293:     pnpm run build
L294:     pnpm dsh web
L295: 
L296: `pnpm run build` prepares the repository artifacts. `pnpm dsh web` uses those built artifacts without rebuilding.
L297: ## Community and support
L298: 
L299:   * Submit feedback or bug reports through cite63†GitHub Discussions .
L300:   * Add the cite72†`dsh-plugin` topic to your plugin repository for discoverability.
L301:   * Join cite148†DeepSeek Harness Discord community†discord.gg .
L302: 
L303: ## Contributing
L304: 
L305: See cite111†CONTRIBUTING.md .
L306: ## Development
L307: 
L308: Start with the cite149†development guide and cite150†architecture documentation .
L309: 
L310: `pnpm run dev:web` builds, serves, and rebuilds client bundles on source edits in one terminal, and `make help` lists the matching Make targets for Web and Desktop; the guide's application commands section owns the full table.
L311: 
L312: For agents, follow cite104†AGENTS.md .
